name: MO-07
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+21 partisan lean strongly favors the incumbent
Burlison has a large financial advantage (~$958K vs ~$34K cash)
Prediction markets price Democratic chances at about 4%
No polling or expert ratings, but fundamentals leave little doubt
model.rationale: Eric Burlison holds a heavily Republican southwest Missouri seat with a decisive money edge and no meaningful outside opposition, while markets give Missi Hesketh only a token chance. The fundamentals point to a comfortable Republican win of roughly 19 points.
model.watch: A major scandal or unexpected incumbent retirement would be the main route to a closer race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Southwest Missouri's 7th District is one of the most Republican seats in the state, with a partisan lean of about 21 points toward the GOP. First-term incumbent Eric Burlison is running for reelection after clearing his primary, facing Democrat Missi Hesketh and a Libertarian candidate.

The financial picture is lopsided: Burlison has raised about $1.5 million and holds nearly $960,000 on hand, while Hesketh has raised roughly $50,000. No outside groups are active against the incumbent, and prediction markets give Democrats only about a 4% chance. With no public polling and no expert raters flagging the race, everything points to a safe Republican hold.
